title: What If All the Bats Vanished?

scenes.text: What if all the bats vanished? The first bill would land on farms.
A bat eats up to three thousand insects nightly, saving US farms at least three point seven billion dollars yearly.
Over the following years, rainforests would regrow more slowly without fruit bats scattering seeds, and agave and bananas lose pollinators.
We have a real test. White-nose syndrome, found in 2006, has killed over five million North American bats.
From 2006 to 2017, counties that lost bats saw pesticide use rise about thirty-one percent, a Science study found.
The same study links that to about thirteen hundred extra infant deaths. Linked, not proven, but silent skies cost something.

description:
What if all the bats vanished?
Bats save US farms at least $3.7 billion a year, and after white-nose syndrome, a 2024 Science study linked bat losses to about 31 percent more pesticide use and more infant deaths.
